messages.subject: factor mean extraction
parts:
Hi all, 

I fitted a multigroup CFA in three groups and would like to carry out downstream analyses with the factors. One of the things I want to do is to get descriptive statistics on the factors such as factor mean. 

So far, I tried computing factor scores in the three groups (after showing measurement invariance), and then computing factor means in each group. I have also tried to extract the parameter estimate from the fitted model object, and I believe that the parameter "Factor ~ 1" means the latent factor mean? In the latter case, one of the groups is the reference group, and the factor mean is 0, whereas the other groups have non-zero values for factor mean. 

From these two approaches, I found that the results are not consistent in terms of which group has higher/lower factor mean. I wonder which approach should i trust more or if there are alternative approaches to getting descriptive statistics on the latent factors?

Thanks a lot!

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: factor mean extraction
parts: Factor scores are either incorrect or indeterminate (that is, partly arbitrary). How indeterminate depends (primarily) on how many indicators and how strong the loadings. By contrast, the factor mean parameter estimates are the estimates most consistent with the means of the observed variables, given the constraints in the model and your supporting assumptions. If you trust the model, then trust the parameter estimates that come from the model.
